item.title: Lewis Hamilton says ‘Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling’ after Rafah visit
item.description:
• F1 driver urges Israel to let aid into Gaza

  • Trip involved tour of facilities with aid workers

Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton said on Wednesday that Israel must allow aid ⁠trucks into Gaza, a day after he visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt.

Hamilton, a seven-time ⁠world champion, arrived ⁠in ​El Arish on Tuesday, where he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it ⁠is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent’s aid warehouses.

item.title: F1 presses ahead with plan to hold season finale in Middle East despite safety concerns
item.description:
• Imola stood down as back-up plan to finish the year

  • Qatar and Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as planned

Imola has been stood down as a back-up plan for the Formula One season finale as the sport pushes ahead with its scheduled Middle East races.

The Italian venue, 20 miles from Bologna, was lined up to replace Abu Dhabi as the final race amid concern over the ongoing conflict in the region.

item.title: ‘Senna was Senna’: Wolff says it is too soon to compare Kimi Antonelli to F1 great
item.description:
• World champion idolises Brazilian who won three titles

  • ‘He’s a Senninha and not a Senna yet,’ says Toto Wolff

Toto Wolff says it is too soon to compare his world champion driver Kimi Antonelli to Ayrton Senna but that the Italian may yet develop into a driver comparable to the Brazilian great whom Antonelli grew up idolising.

Antonelli sealed his first Formula One world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix and with a fifth place at Sunday’s São Paulo Grand Prix helped Mercedes secure their ninth constructors’ championship and their first drivers’ and constructors’ double since 2020.

item.title: ‘Incredible job’: Antonelli praises Mercedes after F1 constructors’ win in Brazil
item.description:
• World champion pays tribute to team at São Paulo GP

  • Norris wins race but says consistency ‘not good enough’

Kimi Antonelli, the new world champion, paid tribute to the 2,500 personnel at his Mercedes team after they secured the F1 constructors’ title in São Paulo, describing them as an amazing group of people.

The race at Interlagos was won by McLaren’s Lando Norris but with Antonelli in fifth and his teammate George Russell in fourth it was enough to seal a first constructors’ title for Mercedes since 2021 and their first drivers’ and constructors’ double since 2020.

item.title: Dominant Lando Norris powers to victory in São Paulo F1 Grand Prix
item.description:
• Mercedes wrap up constructors’ championship

  • Red Bull’s Max Verstappen surges to second place

Lando Norris delivered a masterclass for victory at the São Paulo Grand Prix, taking the flag at a ­meeting marked by a series of ­striking comebacks.

Max ­Verstappen was once more outstanding at Interlagos by taking second from 21st on the grid and for McLaren it was a victory they have sought since mid-season. But of most import was confirmation of a definitive return from the wilderness for Mercedes as they claimed their ninth Formula One constructors’ world championship.

item.title: Alan Jones obituary
item.description:
Australian driver who was the Formula One champion with the Williams team in 1980 and had 12 grand prix victories

“The championship? You take it any way it comes,” said Alan Jones, with typical unsentimental pithiness, after winning a tense Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal in 1980 that made him that year’s Formula One world champion. This came during his third season with the Williams Grand Prix team, after making a promising showing the year before with four race victories.

Jones, who has died aged 80 of cancer, had taken full advantage of the aerodynamic excellence of the new Williams FW07 car, featuring revolutionary “ground effect” technology, which was introduced in the latter part of the 1979 season.

item.title: Lando Norris claims F1 São Paulo GP pole as ‘crazy’ rain disrupts qualifying
item.description:
• McLaren driver fastest ahead of Mercedes duo

  • Antonelli to start on front row alongside Norris

Mastering the most treacherous of conditions at Interlagos, Lando Norris had the edge to take pole position for McLaren at the São Paulo Grand Prix, having bested a downpour that tested every driver. But with more rain predicted for the race on Sunday, it remains wide open from the front to the very back of the grid.

After a qualifying session that took two and a half hours to complete because of delays caused by the heavy rain, Norris came out on top but the grid will be marked by a very mixed-up formation, as a host of drivers took penalties.

item.title: Hamilton v Leclerc: how can Ferrari solve problem of two number one drivers?
item.description:
The Scuderia are hopeful of being in the world championship mix next season but risk puncturing their chances if they can’t corral their men in the cockpits

Going into this weekend’s São Paulo Grand Prix, all indications are that the status quo at Ferrari will no longer suffice for Lewis Hamilton if the Scuderia’s ambition to return their first drivers’ Formula One championship since 2007 is to be taken seriously.

This year’s drivers’ title is already decided with Kimi Antonelli triumphant at the last round in Mexico and Ferrari are looking towards next season where they are hopeful of genuinely being in the mix against the Italian and Mercedes.

item.title: Lewis Hamilton refuses to back down over criticism of teammate Leclerc
item.description:
• Ferrari teammates clashed at Mexico Grand Prix

  • Hamilton: ‘I’ve worked hard to build a relationship with Charles’

Lewis Hamilton has refused to back down over his criticism of his Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc after a flashpoint between the pair at last weekend’s Mexico Grand Prix.

Leclerc and Hamilton were competing with one another at turn four on the opening lap of the race in Mexico last Sunday, with Leclerc attempting to pass his teammate. He went off in doing so and Hamilton’s defence left him vulnerable to being passed by Max Verstappen who went on to win, costing Ferrari a potential one-two.

item.title: Australian F1 world champion Alan Jones dies aged 80
item.description:
• Jones one of just two Australians to win F1 title after triumph in 1980

  • He won 12 grands prix across 10 seasons before retirement in 1986

Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula One world champion, has died aged 80, leading to a string of tributes from across the sport.

Jones won 12 F1 grands prix across his career and became just the second Australian, after Sir Jack Brabham, to be crowned world champion when he claimed the title with Williams in 1980.

item.title: Liverpool owner FSG holds talks over buying majority stake in Cadillac F1 team
item.description:
• Deal would be worth more than £2bn

  • Cadillac are jointly owned by Mark Walter

Liverpool’s owner, Fenway Sports Group, has held talks about buying a majority stake in the Cadillac Formula One team for more than £2bn as Mark Walter continues to sell off his sporting assets amid allegations of insurance fraud.

Cadillac entered F1 this year as a joint venture between General Motors and Walter’s TWG Global, which sold its controlling interest in the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers and a 13% stake in Chelsea this summer, and is also looking to sell Los Angeles Sparks, the WNBA team.

item.title: Wolff hails world champion Antonelli as role model in blast at F1’s ‘entitled moaners’
item.description:
• Mercedes team principal hits out at ‘selfish’ drivers

  • Antonelli says he will keep No 12 on his car next season

The Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, has described his Formula One world champion Kimi Antonelli as a new kind of racing driver who represents the future of the sport, com­paring him scathingly to what he called some of the entitled ­moaners on the grid and declaring “selfless, ruthless” drivers now dead to F1.

Antonelli secured his first world title in Mexico City on Sunday, at 20 years old becoming the ­youngest F1 champion in only his second season in the sport. The ­Italian’s attitude, enthusiasm and sense of fair play have been notable in a revelatory season for a driver so young and Wolff believes he has proved to be a gamechanger in more ways than one.

item.title: How Kimi Antonelli saw off the grid to become F1’s youngest world champion
item.description:
Mercedes driver makes history at 20 years old by exceeding all expectations in only his second season

Before the 2026 season had begun there was something of a consensus within Formula One. Mercedes appeared to have the fastest car and George Russell was favourite for the title. Beside him in what was indeed a dominant Mercedes, his teenage teammate, Kimi Antonelli, was the prodigious talent who was expected to require honing after a tricky rookie season. Said consensus lasted one race, by the sixth it had been turned on its head and Antonelli was squarely on his way to being champion.

Few had doubted that the then 19-year-old Italian would prove to be strong in a car that for the first two-thirds of the season was the class of the field but for Antonelli to come out of the blocks with such verve, aggressive skill and also the judgment and at times maturity of a veteran was revelatory. As the youngest F1 world champion and Italy’s first since Alberto Ascari in 1953, Antonelli made history this year but it was the way he did it which truly caught the eye.

item.title: ‘I’ve cried way too much today’: Kimi Antonelli fights back tears after F1 title win
item.description:
• 20-year-old seals championship after finishing third in Mexico

  • Fellow drivers unite in praise for sport’s youngest ever champion

Having enjoyed a moment he said he would remember forever, an emotional Kimi Antonelli was moved to tears once more in remembering his grandfather after the Italian won the Formula One world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix.

In turn, his fellow drivers were unstinting in their praise for the new champion, who took his debut title with third place at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. Among those was Lewis Hamilton, but the British driver also delivered a stern rebuke to his Ferrari teammate, Charles Leclerc.

item.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GP
item.description:
• 20-year-old clinches title with four races to go

  • Verstappen wins race ahead of Hamilton

Kimi Antonelli etched his name into the Formula One record books as world champion and as a deserved and popular winner whose verve and extraordinary skill has been thrilling to watch, turning what many thought might have been an unlikely title tilt into a triumphant march, sealed with tears of joy at the Mexican Grand Prix.

In taking his debut F1 title for Mercedes, the 20-year-old Antonelli, with his tousled hair and charming boyish looks, is the youngest driver to claim the sport’s crown and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari won in 1953. It is Mercedes’ first drivers’ championship since Hamilton last won in 2020 and the team’s 10th.
